writing.sample_en:
【参考范文 · 174 词】写作无唯一标准答案，以下为达标示范
Nowadays more and more college students have come to realize social practice and academic learning are equally important. Rather than treating them as rivals competing for limited time, an increasing number of us regard the two as partners that reinforce each other, and I firmly share this view.
Academic learning equips us with theories, while social practice tests and deepens them. Knowledge that never leaves the textbook easily fades, yet once applied, it truly takes root. Take my own experience as an example. After studying marketing principles for a whole semester, I joined a campus start-up and helped promote its products online. Only then did the abstract concepts suddenly make sense, and in return the real feedback from customers pushed me back to my books with sharper questions. Learning guided my practice, and practice enriched my learning.
Therefore, academic study and social practice are two wheels of the same cart, and neither can be spared. Only by letting them go hand in hand can college students grow into capable talents that society genuinely needs.

lines.en: M: I've just bought a new blender.
lines.zh: M: 我刚买了一台新搅拌机。

lines.en: W: What's that?
lines.zh: W: 那是什么？

lines.en: M: A blender, you know, a machine that blends food.
lines.zh: M: 搅拌机，你知道，就是一种用来搅拌食物的机器。

lines.en: W: Uh, yes, of course, the electric kitchen appliance.
lines.zh: W: 呃，知道，当然知道，就是那种电动厨房用具。

lines.en: M: Exactly, this one is state-of-the-art. I've been meaning to buy one for a while, and I did thorough research on which specific model to get. I read through maybe hundreds of online user reviews. Anyway, it's amazing.
lines.zh: M: 没错，这台是最先进的。我想买一台已经有一段时间了，而且还认真研究了到底该买哪个具体型号。我大概看了上百条网上的用户评价。总之，它太棒了。

lines.en: W: Really? What could be so special about it? I mean it's just a blender.
lines.zh: W: 真的吗？它到底有什么特别的？我的意思是，它不就是一台搅拌机吗？

lines.en: M: Well, basically, it's just a very good one. It feels heavy and sturdy and well made. It also has lots of power and can easily cut and crush practically anything. This way, the soups and juices I make come out really fine and smooth, with no lumpy bits.
lines.zh: M: 嗯，基本上，它就是一台非常好的搅拌机。拿在手里感觉很重、很结实，做工也很好。它的功率也很大，几乎什么东西都能轻松切碎、碾碎。这样一来，我做出来的汤和果汁都特别细腻顺滑，没有结块。

lines.en: W: Um, I see. I've never thought of getting one myself. It sounds like the kind of thing that, for me personally, I would rarely use.
lines.zh: W: 嗯，我明白了。我从来没想过自己也买一台。听起来，这种东西对我个人来说应该很少会用到。

lines.en: M: I've never had one before, and now that I do. I use it all the time. I make a fresh fruit juice in the morning, maybe not every morning, but three or four times a week, and it feels fantastic. It's a really healthy habit.
lines.zh: M: 我以前从来没有搅拌机，但现在有了以后，我一直在用。我早上会做新鲜果汁，也不是每天早上都做，但每周会做三四次，而且感觉特别棒。这真是个非常健康的习惯。

lines.en: W: I can imagine that must feel quite satisfying. I can picture you getting all creative in the kitchen and trying out a multitude of different ingredient combinations, and it's obviously going to be healthier than buying packaged juice from a supermarket.
lines.zh: W: 我能想象那一定很令人满足。我都能想象你在厨房里发挥创意，尝试各种各样的食材组合，而且这显然会比从超市买包装果汁更健康。

lines.en: M: It's so much healthier. It's not even close. Did you know that store-bought juice is like 10% sugar?
lines.zh: M: 健康多了，根本不是一个级别的。你知道吗，商店里买的果汁含糖量大约是百分之十？

lines.en: W: Right, so then you bought it for the health benefits?
lines.zh: W: 好吧，所以你买它主要是为了健康方面的好处？

lines.en: M: Mostly yes. Basically, it allows me to have a more varied diet with a far wider assortment of nutrients, because it's not only fruit in my morning juices you see. I can also throw in vegetables, nuts, yogurts, cereals, anything that tickles my fancy.
lines.zh: M: 主要是的。基本上，它让我能拥有更加多样化的饮食，摄入种类丰富得多的营养，因为你看，我早上的果汁里可不只是水果。我还可以加蔬菜、坚果、酸奶、谷物，任何我喜欢的东西都行。

lines.en: W: Today we have a very interesting guest. Mr. Thomas Benjamin Grimm, the mayor of Berkton, is here to talk about his job and responsibilities overseeing this charming village. Mr. Grimm, thank you for being here.
lines.zh: W: 今天我们请到了一位非常有趣的嘉宾。伯克顿的市长托马斯·本杰明·格里姆先生来到这里，和我们谈谈他的工作，以及负责管理这个迷人的村庄所承担的责任。格里姆先生，感谢您今天来到这里。

lines.en: M: Thank you for having me.
lines.zh: M: 谢谢您的邀请。

lines.en: W: I'd like to start by stating the obvious. Berkton has become one of the most popular tourist destinations in the country, and this has happened under your watch. Just how did you achieve this?
lines.zh: W: 我想先从一个显而易见的事实说起。伯克顿已经成为全国最受欢迎的旅游目的地之一，而这一切都是在您的任期内发生的。您究竟是如何做到的？

lines.en: M: The achievement belongs to all the residents of Berkton. It was a shared effort where everybody pitched in for the communal good.
lines.zh: M: 这项成就属于伯克顿的所有居民。这是大家共同努力的结果，每个人都为公共利益贡献了自己的力量。

lines.en: W: But how did this change happen? In about 10 years, Berkton has gone from a relatively unheard-of sleepy village to a must-see destination.
lines.zh: W: 但这种变化是如何发生的呢？大约10年的时间里，伯克顿从一个相对默默无闻、寂静沉睡的村庄，变成了一个必游之地。

lines.en: M: Yes, the change has truly been remarkable. Berkton was always fortunate to be endowed with such a beautiful natural allure. The Ambury Hills above the village remain untouched by human development, and the Sonora Valley just below it is equally stunning. The transformation commenced in a town hall meeting in spring 2008 over 10 years ago now, when an overwhelming majority of neighbors voted in favor of "Motion 836". This legislative proposal essentially set out to harmonize the aesthetic appearance of all the houses in Berkton. The idea was that if all the properties looked a certain way with shared design features, then a village as a whole would look more beautiful. And it worked.
lines.zh: M: 是的，这种变化确实非常显著。伯克顿一直很幸运，拥有如此美丽的自然风光。村庄上方的安布里山丘仍未受到人类开发，而下方的索诺拉谷同样美不胜收。这场转变始于十多年前，也就是2008年春天的一次市政厅会议。当时，绝大多数居民投票赞成了“第836号动议”。这项立法提案的核心目标，是让伯克顿所有房屋的外观风格协调统一。这个想法是，如果所有房产都采用某种统一的外观和共同的设计元素，那么整个村庄看起来就会更加美丽。事实证明，这确实奏效了。

lines.en: W: It certainly did. I'm looking now at a before-and-after photo, and the change is truly remarkable. It's hard to believe it's the same place. And how do the neighbors feel now?
lines.zh: W: 确实如此。我现在正在看一张改造前后的照片，这种变化真的非常显著。很难相信这是同一个地方。那么，居民们现在对此有什么感受呢？

lines.en: M: Great pride, I would say.
lines.zh: M: 我想，他们感到非常自豪。

lines.en: W: But what about the multitudes of visitors now crowding the streets? Is everyone happy about that?
lines.zh: W: 但现在有成群的游客挤满街道，这又怎么样呢？大家对此都感到满意吗？

lines.en: M: The tourists we receive are a blessing, as they have completely revitalized our local economy. Every visitor is warmly welcome.
lines.zh: M: 我们迎来的游客是上天的恩赐，因为他们让我们的地方经济彻底恢复了活力。每一位游客都会受到热情欢迎。

lines.en: Researchers in the US have created a remote-controlled robot that is so small it can walk on the top of a US penny. In research published in the journal Science Robotics, a team at Northwestern University said the crab-like robot is 0.5mm wide. Researchers described it as the smallest-ever remote-controlled walking robot.
lines.zh: 美国研究人员研制出一种遥控机器人，小到可以在一枚美国一美分硬币的顶部行走。在《科学机器人学》杂志发表的一项研究中，西北大学的一个团队表示，这种蟹状机器人宽度仅为0.5毫米。研究人员称，这是迄今为止最小的遥控行走机器人。

lines.en: The tiny robot can bend, twist, crawl, walk, turn, and even jump without the use of complex hardware or special power. The engineers said this is because the robot is powered by the elastic property of its body. To construct the robot, the researchers used a shape-memory alloy material that transforms to its remembered shape when heated.
lines.zh: 这种微型机器人无需复杂的硬件或特殊动力，就能弯曲、扭转、爬行、行走、转弯，甚至跳跃。工程师表示，这是因为机器人依靠其身体的弹性特性驱动。为了制造这种机器人，研究人员使用了一种形状记忆合金材料，这种材料受热后会恢复到其记忆中的形状。

lines.en: Using a laser, the team is able to heat the robot at specific parts of its body, causing it to change shape. As the robot deforms and goes back to its original shape, it creates movement from one place to another. "Because these structures are so tiny, the rate of cooling is very fast," project lead Professor John A. Rogers said. "In fact, reducing the sizes of these robots allows them to run faster."
lines.zh: 团队利用激光加热机器人身体的特定部位，使其发生形变。当机器人变形并恢复到原来的形状时，就会产生从一个地方移动到另一个地方的运动。项目负责人约翰·A·罗杰斯教授说：“由于这些结构非常微小，冷却速度非常快。事实上，缩小这些机器人的尺寸可以使它们运行得更快。”

lines.en: While the research is still in the exploratory phase, the team believes that technology could lead to micro-sized robots that can perform practical tasks in tightly confined spaces. "You might imagine micro-robots as agents to repair or assemble small structures or machines in industry or as surgical assistants to clear clogged arteries, to stop internal bleeding, or to eliminate cancerous tumours—all in minimally invasive procedures," Rogers said.
lines.zh: 尽管这项研究仍处于探索阶段，但团队相信，这项技术可能促成能够在极其狭窄空间内执行实际任务的微型机器人。罗杰斯说：“你可以设想，微型机器人可作为执行者，在工业领域维修或组装微小的结构或机器；也可以作为手术助手，在微创手术中清除堵塞的动脉、止住内出血或消除癌性肿瘤。”

lines.en: I don't want to boast or anything, but I have always considered myself something of an elite sleeper. Given the opportunity, I will sleep for marathon stretches, and can doze through the most extreme situations. On one very rough ferry crossing, on the route to the Isles of Scilly, for example, my traveling companion spent the entire 3-hour-ride throwing up in the bathroom, while I dozed happily on a plastic chair.
lines.zh: 我不想自夸什么的，但我一直认为自己算得上是睡眠精英。只要有机会，我就会一睡数小时，甚至在最极端的情况下也能打瞌睡。例如，在一次前往锡利群岛的航线上，渡轮经历了一段非常颠簸的航程，我的同伴在整个3小时的旅途中都待在卫生间里呕吐，而我却惬意地坐在塑料椅上打盹。

lines.en: Unfortunately, it has come to my attention that I am not an elite sleeper after all. It seems I am just lazy, because elite sleepers are defined as the approximately 3 percent of the population who are biologically programmed to need less sleep than the rest of us. According to a study that came out in March, elite sleepers have rare genetic changes, which means they can sleep fewer hours than mere mortals, without any risk of cognitive decline.
lines.zh: 遗憾的是，我最近才意识到自己终究算不上睡眠精英。看来我只是懒，因为睡眠精英的定义是：约占总人口3%、在生理上注定比我们其他人需要更少睡眠的人。根据一项于3月公布的研究，睡眠精英存在罕见的基因变化，这意味着他们睡眠时间少于普通人，却不会面临认知能力下降的风险。

lines.en: It may not be possible to change your own genes, but can you train yourself to need less sleep? Is there a non-biological way to reach elite sleeper status? I have spent the past year trying to answer that question. Not for fun, I should add, but because having a baby has severely disrupted my sleep, for which I still have a great passion.
lines.zh: 改变自己的基因或许不可能，但你能训练自己减少睡眠需求吗？有没有一种非生物学的方法可以成为睡眠精英？过去一年里，我一直在努力回答这个问题。需要补充说明的是，这并不是为了好玩，而是因为生孩子严重打乱了我的睡眠，而我至今仍然非常热爱睡觉。

lines.en: For a while, I assumed I'd be forced to become one of those people who jump out of bed at the crack of dawn. After a year of tough scientific study, however, I have discovered being forced to get up early in the morning is very different from being an early bird.
lines.zh: 有一段时间，我以为自己不得不变成那种天一亮就从床上跳起来的人。然而，经过一年的艰苦科学研究，我发现，被迫早起与早起的人是两回事。

lines.en: If you read an article about a controversial issue, do you think you'd realise if it had changed your beliefs? No one knows your own mind like you do—it seems obvious that you would know if your beliefs had shifted. And yet a new paper in the Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology suggests that we actually have very poor awareness of our own belief change, meaning that we will tend to underestimate how much we've been swayed by a convincing article.
lines.zh: 如果你读了一篇有关争议性问题的文章，你认为自己会意识到它是否改变了你的信念吗？没有人比你更了解自己的想法——你似乎理所当然会知道自己的信念是否发生了变化。然而，《实验心理学季刊》发表的一篇新论文表明，我们实际上很难觉察到自己的信念变化，这意味着我们往往会低估自己受一篇有说服力的文章影响的程度。

lines.en: The researchers recruited over two hundred undergraduates across two studies and focused on their beliefs about whether physical punishment of kids is an effective form of discipline. The students reported their initial beliefs about whether physical punishment is an effective way to discipline a child on a scale from "1" completely disbelieve to "9" completely believe. Several weeks later they were given one of two research-based texts to read: each was several pages long and either presented the arguments and data in favour of physical punishment or against it. After this, the students answered some questions to test their comprehension and memory of the text. Then, the students again scored their belief about whether physical punishment is effective or not. Finally, the researchers asked them to recall what their belief had been at the start of the study.
lines.zh: 研究人员在两项研究中招募了两百多名本科生，重点考察他们对于体罚孩子是否是一种有效管教方式的看法。学生们首先在“1”（完全不相信）到“9”（完全相信）的量表上报告自己对于体罚是否是管教孩子的有效方式的初始看法。几周后，他们被安排阅读两篇基于研究的文章中的一篇：每篇文章都有数页之长，分别陈述支持或反对体罚的论据和数据。读完后，学生们回答了一些问题，以测试他们对文章内容的理解和记忆。随后，学生们再次对自己认为体罚是否有效进行评分。最后，研究人员要求他们回忆研究开始时自己的看法。

lines.en: The students' belief about physical punishment changed when they read a text that argued against their own initial position. Crucially, the memory of their initial belief was shifted in the direction of their new belief—in fact, their memory was closer to their current belief than their original belief. The more their belief had changed, the larger this memory bias tended to be, suggesting the students were relying on their current belief to deduce the initial belief. The memory bias was unrelated to the measures of how well they'd understood or recalled the text, suggesting these factors didn't play a role in memory of initial belief or awareness of belief change.
lines.zh: 当学生们读到一篇主张反对其最初立场的文章时，他们对于体罚的看法发生了变化。关键在于，他们对自己初始看法的记忆也朝着新看法的方向发生了偏移——事实上，他们记忆中的初始看法比起原先的看法，更接近当前的看法。他们的看法变化越大，这种记忆偏差通常也越大，这表明学生们可能是在依靠当前的看法来推断最初的看法。记忆偏差与他们对文章的理解程度或回忆程度无关，这说明这些因素并未影响他们对初始看法的记忆，也未影响他们对信念变化的觉察。

lines.en: The researchers concede that this research was about changes to mostly moderate beliefs—it's likely the findings would be different in the context of changes to extreme or deeply held beliefs. However, our beliefs on most topics are in the moderate range, and as we go about our daily lives reading informative material, these intriguing findings suggest we are mostly ignorant of how what we just read has updated and altered our own position.
lines.zh: 研究人员承认，这项研究考察的是主要处于中等程度的信念变化——如果是在极端或根深蒂固的信念发生变化的情况下，研究结果很可能会有所不同。然而，我们对大多数问题的看法都处于中等范围，而且当我们在日常生活中阅读信息性材料时，这些耐人寻味的发现表明，我们大多没有意识到刚刚读到的内容如何更新并改变了自己的立场。

lines.en: As the American population grows, so does the number of American moms. But, more than a century after Mother's Day became an official holiday, even as that number increases, the share of the American population who are mothers is at the lowest point in a quarter century.
lines.zh: 随着美国人口增长，美国母亲的人数也在增加。但是，在母亲节成为法定节日一个多世纪之后，尽管这一人数不断上升，母亲在美国总人口中所占的比例却处于四分之一世纪以来的最低点。

lines.en: It's frequently noted that fertility rates are falling sharply in richer countries. But the less-observed consequence of this trend is that the decline in births can also mean a decline in motherhood in America. According to my analysis of data from the Census Bureau, the decline of American motherhood is real, occurring very quickly, and may continue for some time yet.
lines.zh: 人们经常注意到，较富裕国家的生育率正在急剧下降。然而，这一趋势一个较少被关注的后果是，出生人数减少也可能意味着美国母亲人数的减少。根据我对人口普查局数据的分析，美国母亲人数的下降确实存在，发生得非常迅速，而且可能还会持续一段时间。

lines.en: Not only are moms making up less of the population, but their characteristics are changing too, and in a way that might be linked to their proportional decline. Moms today tend to be older than in the past. Just looking at recent years, the change in age-specific birth rates has been drastic.
lines.zh: 母亲不仅在总人口中所占的比例越来越低，她们的特征也在发生变化，而且这种变化可能与她们比例上的下降有关。如今的母亲往往比过去年长。仅从近几年来看，不同年龄段的生育率变化就十分显著。

lines.en: In just the past few years, the peak childbearing age range for American women has advanced from that of 25-29 to that of 30-34. Meanwhile, childbearing among women under 20 has fallen by half or more, while childbearing among women 35 and older is rising.
lines.zh: 就在过去几年中，美国女性生育高峰年龄段已从25至29岁推移到30至34岁。同时，20岁以下女性的生育率下降了一半甚至更多，而35岁及以上女性的生育率正在上升。

lines.en: One positive consequence of this age shift is that a larger proportion of new mothers are economically prepared to raise children. Less positively, however, many women find that, as they age, they can't have as many kids as they would like. Plus, having children later in life can increase the risk of health complications. These finer points aside, one major consequence of the older-moms trend is that fewer years of a woman's life are spent as a mother. This means that, at any given time, a larger share of women, and thus of the whole population, will report not having children in government surveys. In other words, later motherhood means less motherhood.
lines.zh: 这一年龄变化带来的一个积极后果是，新生母亲中有更大比例在经济上已做好抚养孩子的准备。然而，不那么积极的是，许多女性发现，随着年龄增长，她们无法生育自己希望拥有的那么多孩子。此外，晚年生育还会增加出现健康并发症的风险。撇开这些更细致的问题不谈，母亲年龄增长趋势的一个主要后果是，女性一生中作为母亲度过的年数减少了。这意味着，在任何特定时点，接受政府调查的女性中，以及因此在全部人口中，报告自己没有孩子的人所占比例都会更高。换句话说，晚育意味着较少的母亲经历。

lines.en: Even as motherhood rates decline, Mother's Day, of course, will endure. In fact, despite the demographic shift, retail spending on the holiday appears to be rising. It is hard to say if Mother's Day spending is rising more than one would expect, given that the American population keeps growing, but one factor might be that the proportion of women who are the mothers of adult children is rising. And those adult children may spend more generously when it comes to celebrating the moms they no longer live with.
lines.zh: 即使母亲比例正在下降，母亲节当然仍将延续下去。事实上，尽管人口结构发生了变化，这一节日的零售消费似乎正在增加。很难说母亲节消费的增长是否超出了美国人口持续增长这一因素所能带来的预期，但其中一个原因可能是，成年子女的母亲在女性中的比例正在上升。而这些成年子女在庆祝那些已经不再与自己共同生活的母亲时，可能会更加慷慨。

lines.en: Since NASA published a paper in 1989 claiming that houseplants can soak up pollution and toxic chemicals, businesses and homeowners have increasingly invested in greenery to help clean their air. But, a new analysis suggests it could actually take more than 1,000 plants per square meter to gain a benefit any greater than simply opening a couple of windows.
lines.zh: 自美国国家航空航天局（NASA）于1989年发表一篇论文，声称室内植物能够吸收污染物和有毒化学物质以来，企业和房主越来越多地投资于绿植，以帮助净化空气。然而，一项新的分析表明，要获得任何超过简单打开几扇窗户所能带来的益处，实际上可能需要每平方米摆放超过1000株植物。

lines.en: The problem lies in the fact that NASA conducted their tests in sealed containers that do not simulate the conditions in most people's homes or offices. The space agency was primarily concerned about keeping the air fresh for astronauts cut off in biospheres or space stations and helping to combat "sick building syndrome", which had become a problem due to the super insulated and energy efficient offices of the late 1970s. By the early 1980s, workers regularly complained of skin rashes, sleeplessness, headaches, and allergies as they breathed in toxic chemicals from paints and plastics.
lines.zh: 问题在于，NASA是在密封容器中进行测试的，而这种环境并不能模拟大多数人家中或办公室的实际情况。该航天机构主要关注的是如何为被隔绝在生物圈或空间站中的宇航员保持空气清新，以及帮助应对“病态建筑综合征”。由于20世纪70年代末的办公室采用了高度隔热且节能的设计，这种综合征逐渐成为一个问题。到了20世纪80年代初，员工经常抱怨出现皮疹、失眠、头痛和过敏症状，因为他们吸入了来自油漆和塑料的有毒化学物质。

lines.en: NASA found that certain plants could remove chemicals from the air, and even today, garden centers recommend the plants for air cleaning properties. However, a new evaluation of dozens of studies spanning 30 years found that houseplants in a normal environment have little impact. In fact, natural ventilation is far better at cleaning the air. The researchers also calculated the clean air delivery rate for plants in the studies they analyzed and found that the rate at which plants disperse the compounds was well below the usual rate of air exchange in a normal building, caused by the movement of people coming and going, opening doors and windows.
lines.zh: NASA发现，某些植物能够去除空气中的化学物质，直到今天，园艺中心仍会因这些植物具有净化空气的功效而予以推荐。然而，一项对历时30年、涵盖数十项研究的新评估发现，在正常环境中，室内植物的影响微乎其微。事实上，自然通风在净化空气方面要有效得多。研究人员还计算了所分析研究中植物的清洁空气输送率，发现植物分散这些化合物的速率远低于普通建筑通常的空气交换速率；后者是由人员进出以及开关门窗等活动造成的。

lines.en: Many of the studies did show a reduction in the concentration of volatile organic compounds over time, which is likely why people have seized on them to praise the air purifying virtues of plants. But the researchers' calculation showed it would take 10 to 1,000 plants per square meter of floor space to compete with the air cleaning capacity of a building's air handling system or even just a couple of open windows in a house. In contrast, NASA's sealed experiment recommended one pot plant per 100 square feet.
lines.zh: 许多研究确实显示，挥发性有机化合物的浓度会随着时间推移而降低，这可能就是人们抓住这一点来赞美植物净化空气功效的原因。但研究人员的计算表明，要与建筑空气处理系统，甚至住宅中仅仅打开几扇窗户的空气净化能力相匹敌，每平方米地面面积需要摆放10至1000株植物。相比之下，NASA的密封实验建议每100平方英尺摆放一盆植物。

lines.en: This is certainly an example of how scientific findings can be misleading or misinterpreted over time. But it's also a great example of how scientific research should continually reexamine and question findings to get closer to the ground truth of understanding what's actually happening.
lines.zh: 这无疑说明，科学发现可能会随着时间推移而产生误导或被误解。但这也很好地体现了科学研究应当不断重新审视并质疑已有发现，从而更加接近对实际情况的真实理解。

analysis.定位: P3 However, a new evaluation of dozens of studies spanning 30 years found that houseplants in a normal environment have little impact. In fact, natural ventilation is far better at cleaning the air. 然而，一项跨越 30 年、对数十项研究的新评估发现，正常环境下的室内植物作用甚微。事实上，自然通风在净化空气方面要好得多。
analysis.信号: However 转折后是真结论。However, a new evaluation 用 However 把语气从『植物有用』扭向新结论，转折之后的两句才是答案落点，尤其 In fact, natural ventilation is far better 是核心。

questions.stem: 【题目】 What does NASA's sealed experiment recommendation exemplify in scientists' pursuit of truth?
questions.stem_zh: NASA的密封实验建议在科学家追求真理的过程中体现了什么?

analysis.定位: P5 This is certainly an example of how scientific findings can be misleading or misinterpreted over time. But it's also a great example of how scientific research should continually reexamine and question findings to get closer to the ground truth of understanding what's actually happening. 这无疑是一个例子，说明科学发现如何会随时间被误导或误读。但它也是一个绝佳的例子，说明科学研究应当不断重新审视、质疑已有结论，以更接近事情真相的理解。
analysis.信号: But also 转向真正落点。结尾两句用 But it's also a great example of 把重点从『发现会被误读』转到『科研应不断重审质疑』；题干问 pursuit of truth（追求真理），对应的正是 But 之后这句升华。
analysis.替换: scientific research should continually reexamine and question findings↔The necessity of continually reexamining and challenging findings.should=necessity，question=challenging
analysis.排除: A)与原文相反The root cause for misinterpretations of scientific findings. 抓的是 But 之前那句 can be misleading or misinterpreted，且录音只说会被误读、从未分析『根本原因（root cause）』，既取错重心又无中生有。 借用原文：how scientific findings can be misleading or misinterpreted over time B)原词陷阱The difficulty in understanding what's actually happening. 盗用了录音结尾 understanding what's actually happening 这串原词，却把它说成『理解之难（difficulty）』；录音说的是科研应不断质疑以『接近』真相，重点是方法而非『难』，属截取原词答非所问。 借用原文：to get closer to the ground truth of understanding what's actually happening C)未提及The steps to be taken in arriving at any conclusion with certainty. 说『下确定结论的步骤』，录音强调的恰恰是『不断重审质疑、逼近真相』这种开放过程，并未给出『确定结论的步骤』，且 certainty 与录音口吻相反，属未提及兼相反。

cloze.title: 2024年6月·第2套 英语六级完形填空（选词填空） · 26–35 题答案与解析

passages.en: The Sun Is Also a Star is a truly lovely story of love, romance, fate, and destiny.
passages.zh: 《太阳也是一颗星星》是一部真正动人的关于爱情、浪漫、命运和宿命的故事。

passages.en: Natasha is a Jamaican-born immigrant living __(26)__ in America, not by choice exactly. Her parents brought her over and created the situation she __(27)__ to be out of.
passages.zh: 娜塔莎出生于牙买加，是一名生活在美国的非法移民，但这并不完全是她自己的选择。她的父母把她带到美国，造成了如今的处境，而她一直努力想摆脱这种处境。

passages.en: Daniel is an American born of Korean immigrants. He believes in true love, fate, and all that other nonsense that Natasha __(28)__ through scientific reasoning.
passages.zh: 丹尼尔出生在美国，父母是韩国移民。他相信真爱、命运，以及其他所有那些被娜塔莎用科学推理加以否定的无稽之谈。

passages.en: Daniel and Natasha meet by __(29)__ on the streets of New York on the day that she is to be __(30)__ . She doesn't tell him that but does allow him to keep her company while he tries to get her to fall in love with him over the course of the day.
passages.zh: 丹尼尔和娜塔莎在纽约街头偶然相遇，那天正是她即将被驱逐出境的日子。她没有告诉他这件事，却允许他陪着自己，而他则试图在这一天里让她爱上自己。

passages.en: Natasha is me. I found her so similar to myself. She's scientifically-minded, practical, somewhat cynical, and always __(31)__ . Her obsession with the universe through a scientific lens is infectious and I __(32)__ Daniel seeing that too.
passages.zh: 娜塔莎就是我。我发现她和自己非常相像。她以科学为思维基础，务实，多少有些愤世嫉俗，而且总是持怀疑态度。她透过科学的视角痴迷于宇宙，而我非常喜欢丹尼尔也能看到这一点。

passages.en: Daniel is charming and passionate and has a way with words that even __(33)__ Natasha's tough outer shell. By the end of the book I fell in love with both of them.
passages.zh: 丹尼尔迷人而热情，而且很会说话，甚至能打破娜塔莎坚硬的外壳。读到书的结尾时，我已经爱上了他们两个人。

passages.en: I used to find romance stories to always be cheap or laughable. I think now I can see the value in escaping into a story of pure optimism. I got __(34)__ in The Sun Is Also a Star and finished it cover to cover in a weekend. I couldn't wait to get to what I hoped would be a happy ending.
passages.zh: 过去我总觉得爱情故事既廉价又可笑。但现在，我想我开始明白了，沉浸在一个充满纯粹乐观主义的故事中逃离现实，也是有价值的。我沉浸在《太阳也是一颗星星》中，一个周末从头到尾读完了这本书。我迫不及待地想看到我所希望的那个美满结局。

passages.en: It's nice every once in a while to give in to magic. It doesn't have to be a hard fantasy novel with actual spells, it can be the magic found between two people who just have that special something. That __(35)__ that causes them to react and spark when they're near each other.
passages.zh: 偶尔向魔法屈服一次也很好。它不一定非得是一本有真正咒语的奇幻小说，也可以是存在于两个人之间的那种魔法：他们之间有某种特别的东西，那种化学反应会让他们在彼此靠近时产生反应并迸发火花。

wordbank.gloss: 动词第三人称单数：攻击；名词复数：袭击
化学；人与人之间的默契、火花
动词第三人称单数：使破裂、攻破；名词复数：裂缝
驱逐出境（过去式/过去分词），可作被动结构中的过去分词
第三人称单数：不予理会、驳回、解雇
lose 的过去式/过去分词；形容词：迷失的、沉浸的（get lost in 沉浸于）
规定的、开（药）的（过去式/过去分词）
第三人称单数：努力、奋斗（常与 to do 搭配）

rows.text: I) illegally副词
living 后缺修饰语，需副词
与下句「想脱离的处境」呼应=非法滞留 紧接着的 Her parents brought her over and created the situation she __(27)__ to be out of. 说明父母带她过来、造成了她想摆脱的「处境」——这种典型「移民却想脱身」的处境就是「非法居留」。illegally 修饰 living，正好把这条暗线一句话点透。
K)perpetually语义不指向她想脱离的困境 perpetually=「永久地」只描述时间长度，无法解释她「想 be out of」的那种处境，与后文的脱身意愿不咬合。
O) strives动词
she 后缺谓语 + to be 不定式
strive to be out of=努力摆脱 Natasha 想摆脱「非法居留即将被遣返」的处境，strives to be out of 正好表达「她一直在努力跳出这处境」的奋斗感，与全文中她「practical、cynical、scientifically-minded」的人物形象一致。
H) dismisses动词
定语从句中 Natasha 后缺谓语
dismiss=不予理会、驳回 她对 Daniel 那些「真爱、命运」之类的「nonsense（胡说八道）」用「scientific reasoning（科学推理）」来对待——最贴的就是「dismiss=驳回 / 不予理会」。一个 skeptical 的人对超验信念的标准反应就是 dismiss。

C)assaults攻击太过激烈，搭配也不自然 assault 一般指人身/语言上的猛烈攻击，「用科学推理 assault 胡话」搭配生硬、语气也过激，不像理性书评的写法。 F)crackscrack 通常指「攻破壳/裂开」，留给 33 题 crack 的「击破外壳」义更贴合 33 题 that even __(33)__ Natasha's tough outer shell 那种「攻破她那层硬壳」的形象化表达，把它放在这里会和那条线抢词。
最具迷惑性的错误词是 F) —— cracks 极易被误填到 28。cracks 也是 -s 动词、也能搭「攻破 nonsense」，但它真正的家在 33 题的 outer shell；若 28 用了 cracks，33 题就只能勉强配 assaults，全篇逻辑塌方。防坑口诀：看到 outer shell/wall 这种 metaphor 宾语，先把 crack 留给它。
E) coincidence名词
介词 by 后接名词
by coincidence=偶然地，固定搭配 by coincidence 是英语里非常稳定的方式状语短语，意为「偶然、巧合地」；正好对应 The Sun Is Also a Star is a truly lovely story of love, romance, fate, and destiny. 里反复出现的「命运」基调——两个陌生人街头偶遇、命中注定的故事开端。
D)chemistry搭配不立 + 语义留给最后一空 by chemistry 不是英语固定搭配；而且 chemistry「人与人之间的默契火花」更适合留给 35 题里 That __(35)__ that causes them to react and spark when they're near each other. 那种「化学反应」语义。
G) deported动词
be to be __(30)__ 是被动不定式
与 26 题非法居留对应=即将被驱逐 26 题已经定下 Natasha 是 Natasha is a Jamaican-born immigrant living __(26)__ in America 非法身份；那么「她今天即将 be __(30)__」最合逻辑的就是「被驱逐出境」（deported），整本书最大的戏剧张力——一日相恋、当晚遣返——也由此而来。
L)prescribed语义指向开药/规定，不切人物处境 prescribed=「被规定 / 被开药」，与一个非法移民、纽约街头偶遇的剧情语境完全脱节，属于看着是过去分词却被语义淘汰。
N) skeptical形容词
she is 的并列表语

与 scientifically-minded、cynical 同向 skeptical「怀疑论的」与前面 scientifically-minded（科学头脑）、cynical（愤世）属于同一族——理性、不轻信。下一段 He believes in true love, fate, and all that other nonsense that Natasha __(28)__ through scientific reasoning. 也再次印证她「凡事用科学理性质疑」。
M)shrewdshrewd 是「精明」，与「不信」无关 shrewd 形容人「精明、商业上敏锐」，更偏褒义的判断力强，跟前文「scientifically-minded、cynical」的「怀疑、不轻信」语义族对不上。
A) adore动词
主语 I 后缺谓语
adore + sb. + doing=超爱看到某人做某事 上一句 Her obsession with the universe through a scientific lens is infectious 说 Natasha 的科学痴迷有感染力，下半句作者把这种感染对象指向 Daniel——「我超爱看到 Daniel 也被感染到」，adore 的强烈正面色彩与「infectious」呼应。
F) cracks动词
even 后缺谓语动词

cracks + tough outer shell=攻破硬壳 宾语是 Natasha's tough outer shell，「攻破/凿穿坚硬外壳」是 crack 最经典的形象化用法，整句意为「他的口才连 Natasha 那层硬壳都能凿开」，与后文 By the end of the book I fell in love with both of them. 「连读者都被打动」的渐入佳境呼应。
C)assaultsassault 侧重粗暴攻击，色彩负面 assault 带粗暴、敌意色彩，把魅力四射的 Daniel 描述成「攻击」Natasha，与下文「fell in love」的浪漫基调完全冲突。
J) lost形容词
got + 空 + in 表「沉浸于」
get lost in=沉浸于一本书 下文 and finished it cover to cover in a weekend. I couldn't wait to get to what I hoped would be a happy ending. 描写「一个周末从头读到尾、迫不及待想看结局」，正是沉浸阅读的典型表现，与 get lost in 的「沉浸」义完全合拍。
D) chemistry名词
That + 空 + that 定语从句
chemistry=人际默契、火花 chemistry 在英语口语里专指「两个人之间那种说不清的化学反应、默契」，正好对应空后从句 that causes them to react and spark when they're near each other.「让他们一靠近就互相反应、迸出火花」——「react/spark」本身就是化学动词族，互为线索。

最具迷惑性的错误词是 E) —— coincidence 易被反误填到 35。若考生先做 35 题，看到「That __ that causes them to react and spark」可能因「巧合让他们相遇」就误填 coincidence；但 coincidence 与 react/spark 这条化学线索不搭，且 29 题 by + 名词更专属于它。防坑口诀：35 处的同族线索词（react/spark）只对应 chemistry。

longreading.title: 2024年6月·第2套 英语六级长篇阅读（信息匹配） 第 1 篇 · 36–45 题答案与解析

passages.en: A) According to recent research, behavioral change involves physical changes in the brain. In the past decade, researchers have shown that when it comes to the duration of making a new behavior a deep-rooted habit there is not a simple answer. Even for the most productive and disciplined among us, undoing something that has become an automatic part of who we are takes more than an overnight effort. Once we've successfully made that change, we then have to make other adjustments to our lives to ensure that we continue to maintain it, which is often a whole other challenge in itself.
passages.zh: 根据近期研究，行为改变涉及大脑的生理变化。在过去十年中，研究人员已经表明，说到让一种新行为成为根深蒂固的习惯，并没有一个简单的答案。即使对于我们当中最具效率、最自律的人来说，改掉某件已经成为自身自动化组成部分的事情，也需要付出一夜之间无法完成的努力。一旦我们成功做出改变，随后还必须对生活进行其他调整，以确保继续保持这种改变，而这本身往往又是一个完全不同的挑战。

passages.en: B) At its core, success in changing and maintaining a behavior rarely occurs without the introduction of some sort of system. When there isn't the right framework in place, we face a greater likelihood of derailing our hard-earned progress. To ensure success in changing and maintaining a behavior, we should stay away from some detrimental habits.
passages.zh: 从根本上说，如果不建立某种系统，改变并保持一种行为很少能够成功。当没有恰当的框架时，我们辛苦取得的进展更有可能偏离轨道。为了确保改变并保持一种行为取得成功，我们应当避开一些有害的习惯。

passages.en: C) The first one to avoid is relying on willpower. Think about the last time you vowed to resist a temptation. Perhaps you didn't want to check your phone every 15 minutes, or you were determined not to reach for a chocolate bar at 3 p. m. Think about how difficult it must have been not to glance at your phone when it was within reach, or not to walk to the vending machine when your afternoon slump hit.
passages.zh: 首先应避免的是依赖意志力。想想你上一次发誓要抵制诱惑的时候。也许你不想每隔15分钟就查看手机，或者你下定决心下午3点不要伸手去拿巧克力棒。想想看，当手机就在手边时，不瞥一眼它该有多难；或者当午后低迷期袭来时，不走到自动售货机旁该有多难。

passages.en: D) The research on whether we have finite or infinite willpower is inconclusive, but experts do generally agree that you can't change and sustain a habit if you rely on your willpower alone. The old military saying "You never rise to the occasion, you only sink to the level of training" also applies to behavior change. The idea is simple—you repeat something so many times that it becomes automatic.
passages.zh: 关于我们的意志力是有限的还是无限的，相关研究尚无定论，但专家们普遍认同，如果只依靠意志力，就无法改变并维持一种习惯。那句古老的军队格言“你永远不会在关键时刻超越自己的水平，你只会下滑到训练所达到的水平”，同样适用于行为改变。道理很简单：你反复做某件事，次数多到它变成自动化行为。

passages.en: E) Think about what else you can change about your surrounding that makes it easier for you to perform this change on a daily basis. This is called your "cue." Basically, it's a trigger to perform that particular habit. If you don't want to reach for a sugary treat at 3 p. m. , have a box of herbal tea ready at your desk. When 3 p. m. comes around, that's your cue to pour yourself a cup of hot water and drink that tea, instead of walking to the vending machine.
passages.zh: 想想你还可以改变周围环境中的哪些因素，从而让自己更容易每天完成这种改变。这被称为你的“提示”。基本上，它就是促使你执行某种特定习惯的触发因素。如果你不想在下午3点伸手去拿含糖零食，就在办公桌上准备好一盒花草茶。下午3点到来时，这就是提示，提醒你给自己倒一杯热水，喝那杯茶，而不是走到自动售货机旁。

passages.en: F) The second one to avoid is focusing on negative goals. Sometimes, it's not your process that lets you down, but the habit that you want to change in the first place. For starters, not eating chocolate to beat your afternoon slump is a harder goal than swapping chocolate for herbal tea when you reach the designated time. Your brain wants to find routines that have succeeded in the past and allow you to repeat those actions again in the future without having to think about them explicitly. However, this habit-learning system isn't so effective when it comes to learning not to do something. That's why rather than giving up something, think about introducing something in its place. Focus on actions you are going to take that will ultimately conflict with the behaviors you want to stop. When your attention is on doing something new, you give your habit system a chance to operate.
passages.zh: 第二应避免的是专注于消极目标。有时，让你失望的并不是你的过程，而是你一开始就想改变的那个习惯。首先，在午后低迷期不吃巧克力，比在规定时间到来时用花草茶替代巧克力更难实现。你的大脑想要寻找过去曾经成功的惯例，并让你在未来再次重复这些行为，而不必明确地思考它们。然而，在学习不做某件事时，这套习惯学习系统并不那么有效。因此，与其放弃某样东西，不如考虑用另一种东西来取代它。专注于你将要采取的行动，这些行动最终会与那些你想停止的行为发生冲突。当你的注意力集中在做新的事情上时，你就给了自己的习惯系统一个发挥作用的机会。

passages.en: G) The third one to avoid is using the same strategies in different circumstances. Because we are creatures of habit, it's natural to assume that when we do manage to adopt and sustain a desirable behavior, that same strategy will work when we want to make another behavior change. But that's not always the case. Sometimes, the system that got you to change one behavior might not work for another.
passages.zh: 第三应避免的是在不同情境下使用相同的策略。由于我们是习惯性动物，很自然会认为，当我们确实成功养成并保持一种理想行为时，同样的策略也会在我们想改变另一种行为时奏效。但情况并不总是如此。有时，促使你改变一种行为的系统，可能并不适用于另一种行为。

passages.en: H) Sometimes we become accustomed to relying on our guts when it comes to decision-making. This serves us well in certain situations, but can hinder us in others especially when we need to consider metrics and data, rather than letting our instinct override everything. For example, if you want to stop checking your email first thing in the morning, you might decide to substitute another activity in its place. But if you want to stop indulging in video games, simply deciding you will go for a run might not be as effective. You might need to introduce another reinforcement, such as meeting a friend and booking an exercise class together.
passages.zh: 有时，在做决定时，我们会习惯于依靠直觉。在某些情况下，这对我们很有帮助，但在另一些情况下却可能阻碍我们，尤其是当我们需要考虑指标和数据，而不是让本能压倒一切时。例如，如果你想停止早晨一起床就查看电子邮件，你可能会决定用另一项活动来替代它。但如果你想停止沉溺于电子游戏，仅仅决定去跑步可能并不那么有效。你可能需要引入另一种强化因素，比如约一位朋友见面，并一起预约一节锻炼课。

passages.en: I) The fourth one to avoid is not forgiving ourselves for slipping up. Of course, even the best-laid plans fail sometimes. You might have stuck to your screen-free nighttime routine for five days, and then a big project landed on your desk and you found yourself in bed with your laptop before you went to sleep. Or you prepared meals on Sunday and stuck to eating healthy dinners at home, but by Friday you found yourself so exhausted and opted to order greasy takeout. Life happens and even if your behavior change is small, every single day can prove pretty inflexible, and at some point your luck may run out, even if just for a day. The perfectionist in you might be screaming to abandon your goals altogether, but try to see it in the bigger picture. Just because you might have temporarily strayed off course doesn't mean you can't start afresh the next day.
passages.zh: 第四应避免的是在偶尔失误后不原谅自己。当然，即使是最周密的计划有时也会失败。你可能连续五天坚持了夜间不看屏幕的日常安排，随后一个大型项目落到你的办公桌上，于是你发现自己在入睡前躺在床上使用笔记本电脑。或者，你在周日准备好了饭菜，坚持在家吃健康晚餐，但到了周五，你发现自己疲惫不堪，于是选择点油腻的外卖。生活总会发生各种事情，即使你的行为改变很小，每一天也可能相当不容变通；在某个时候，你的好运可能会用尽，哪怕只是一天。你内心的完美主义者可能会大声叫嚷着要彻底放弃目标，但要试着从更大的整体角度来看待这件事。即使你可能暂时偏离了方向，也不意味着你不能在第二天重新开始。

passages.en: J) The final one to avoid is discounting small progress. There's a habit that many perfectionists tend to fall into when they try to establish a behavior change. They focus too much on the big goal and don't take the time to celebrate the small progress they make in the process. Your brain responds to rewards. The basal ganglia, the brain region linked to our performance of habits, is most active at the beginning of a behavior, when the habit is cued, and at the end, when it's rewarded. Say your goal is to run five miles three times a week, and this week you ran one mile on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. Rather than focusing on how far you've gone toward your goal, think about how you can reward yourself for the progress you've made. It doesn't have to be big or expensive; it can be something as simple as making your favorite fruit juice after your run. Whatever your reward, it has to be more than just the activity itself to get you going.
passages.zh: 最后应避免的是忽视微小的进步。许多完美主义者在尝试建立行为改变时，往往会陷入一种习惯。他们过于关注大的目标，却没有花时间庆祝自己在过程中取得的小进步。你的大脑会对奖励作出反应。基底神经节是与我们执行习惯相关的大脑区域，它在行为开始时，也就是习惯受到提示时，以及行为结束时，也就是获得奖励时，最为活跃。假设你的目标是每周跑步三次、每次五英里，而这周你在周一、周三和周五各跑了一英里。与其关注自己距离目标还有多远，不如想想如何奖励自己已经取得的进步。奖励不必贵重或昂贵；它可以简单到在跑步后为自己制作一杯最喜欢的果汁。无论奖励是什么，它都必须不只是活动本身，这样才能促使你行动起来。

passages.en: K) Initiating a new behavior usually seems like the hardest part of the process of change. However, people often fail to adequately prepare for maintaining it. One of the reasons for this is because we mistakenly believe the strategies we used to initiate the change will be equally effective in helping us continue the change. But they won't. Where changing a strongly deep-rooted habit requires changing our belief about that habit that penetrates deeply into our lives, continually manifesting that wisdom requires that we maintain a positive outlook. If our mood is low, the wisdom to behave differently seems to disappear and we go back to eating more and exercising less. The key, then, to maintaining new behaviors is to be happy! Which is why it's so hard to maintain new behaviors.
passages.zh: 开始一种新行为通常看起来是改变过程中最困难的部分。然而，人们往往没有为保持这种行为做好充分准备。其中一个原因是，我们错误地认为，用来启动改变的策略同样能够有效地帮助我们继续改变。但事实并非如此。改变一种根深蒂固的习惯，需要改变我们对这种习惯的看法，因为这种看法已经深入我们的生活；而要持续践行这种认识，则要求我们保持积极的心态。如果情绪低落，采取不同方式行事的智慧似乎就会消失，我们又会回到吃得更多、锻炼得更少的状态。因此，保持新行为的关键就是保持快乐！这也正是维持新行为如此困难的原因。

passages.en: L) Remember, overcoming the behavioral inertia that prevents us from implementing new changes, like eating a healthy diet or exercising, can benefit us in the long run and can improve our physical and mental health. No one was born with habits. They were all learned, and can all, therefore, be unlearned. The question is: how badly do you really want to change?
passages.zh: 记住，克服阻碍我们实施新改变的行为惯性，例如坚持健康饮食或进行锻炼，从长远来看能够使我们受益，并改善我们的身心健康。没有人天生就有习惯。所有习惯都是后天习得的，因此也都可以被改掉。问题在于：你究竟有多么想要改变？

statements.en: There is general consensus among experts that willpower alone cannot guarantee one's success in changing and maintaining a habit.
statements.zh: 专家们普遍认为,仅凭意志力无法保证一个人在改变和保持习惯方面取得成功。

analysis.定位: D 段 The research on whether we have finite or infinite willpower is inconclusive, but experts do generally agree that you can't change and sustain a habit if you rely on your willpower alone. 关于我们意志力是有限还是无限的研究尚无定论，但专家们普遍同意：单靠意志力，你无法改变并维持一个习惯。
analysis.改写: general consensus among experts↔experts do generally agree 名词化同义替换 willpower alone cannot guarantee one's success in changing and maintaining a habit↔you can't change and sustain a habit if you rely on your willpower alone 条件-结果句式重构
analysis.辨邻: C Think about the last time you vowed to resist a temptation只是描写场景，并没有出现题干所要求的general consensus among experts，因此不是答案段。 Think about how difficult it must have been not to glance at your phone when it was within reach

statements.en: One need not abandon their goals completely just because they missed their target temporarily; they can start anew.
statements.zh: 一个人不必仅仅因为暂时错过了目标就完全放弃自己的目标;他们可以重新开始。

statements.en: Research shows it is quite another challenge to maintain a behavioral change after you have initiated it.
statements.zh: 研究表明,在启动行为改变之后,保持这种行为改变是一个完全不同的挑战。

analysis.定位: A 段 Once we've successfully made that change, we then have to make other adjustments to our lives to ensure that we continue to maintain it, which is often a whole other challenge in itself. 一旦我们成功完成了改变，接下来还要对生活做出其他调整以确保能够继续维持，而这往往本身就是另一道难题。
analysis.改写: Research shows↔According to recent research 同义词替换 it is quite another challenge to maintain a behavioral change after you have initiated it↔we then have to make other adjustments to our lives to ensure that we continue to maintain it, which is often a whole other challenge in itself 短语同义 + 时序改写
analysis.辨邻: K K段以Initiating a new behavior usually seems like the hardest part of the process of change开场，谈维持难，但归因是策略与情绪，且不挂"研究"招牌，与题干Research shows不符。 Initiating a new behavior usually seems like the hardest part of the process of change. However, people often fail to adequately prepare for maintaining it.

statements.en: It is wrong to assume the strategies we use to start a change of behavior will work equally well in helping maintain it.
statements.zh: 假设我们用来启动行为改变的策略在帮助保持这种改变方面同样有效是错误的。

analysis.锚点: strategies to start a change won't work for maintaining

analysis.改写: It is wrong to assume the strategies we use to start a change of behavior will work equally well in helping maintain it↔we mistakenly believe the strategies we used to initiate the change will be equally effective in helping us continue the change It is wrong to assume = mistakenly believe

statements.en: Sometimes, it may not be successful to simply substitute one activity with another to effect a change of habit; you may need extra reinforcement.
statements.zh: 有时候,仅仅用一种活动替代另一种活动来实现习惯改变可能并不成功;你可能需要额外的强化。

analysis.锚点: substitute one activity with another + extra reinforcement

You might need to introduce another reinforcement, such as meeting a friend and booking an exercise class together. 但如果你想戒掉沉迷电子游戏，仅仅决定去跑步未必有效；你可能需要引入另一种强化手段，比如约朋友一起报一节锻炼课。
analysis.改写: it may not be successful to simply substitute one activity with another to effect a change of habit↔simply deciding you will go for a run might not be as effective 委婉否定同义 you may need extra reinforcement↔You might need to introduce another reinforcement extra=another（同义替换）

statements.en: One should introduce something new to replace an old habit instead of simply kicking it.
statements.zh: 一个人应该引入新的东西来替代旧习惯,而不是简单地戒掉它。

analysis.锚点: introduce something new to replace an old habit
analysis.定位: F 段 That's why rather than giving up something, think about introducing something in its place. 这就是为什么与其放弃某个东西，不如想想引入新东西去取代它。

statements.en: It is of great benefit to us in the long term to conquer the inertia that stops us from making behavioral changes.
statements.zh: 从长远来看,克服阻止我们做出行为改变的惰性对我们大有裨益。

analysis.锚点: long term benefit + conquer the inertia

analysis.锚点: strategy that changed one behavior may not work for another
analysis.定位: G 段 Sometimes, the system that got you to change one behavior might not work for another. 有时候，让你改变某种行为成功的那个系统，对另一种行为未必有效。

statements.zh: 没有愉快的心情,我们采用不同行为的智慧似乎就会消失。

analysis.锚点: without a happy mood + wisdom vanishes
analysis.定位: K 段 If our mood is low, the wisdom to behave differently seems to disappear and we go back to eating more and exercising less. 如果心情低落，那种采取另一种行为的智慧仿佛就消失了，我们又会回到多吃少动的状态。

passages.en: The "American Dream" promises that in the Land of Opportunity, any individual can climb the economic ladder and prosper through hard work and ambition alone. And yet, young Americans today are struggling to earn more than their parents did at the same age, and upward mobility in the US actually compares unfavourably to that of other industrialised nations.
passages.zh: “美国梦”承诺，在这片机遇之地，任何个人都可以仅凭勤奋和抱负攀登经济阶梯并实现富足。然而，如今的美国年轻人正努力争取在同龄时挣得比父母更多，而美国的向上流动性实际上比其他工业化国家更差。

passages.en: So why does the idea of the American Dream persist? A new study in the American Journal of Political Science identifies one factor that has been overlooked: the influence of reality TV.
passages.zh: 那么，为什么美国梦这一理念仍然存在？《美国政治学杂志》发表的一项新研究指出了一个此前被忽视的因素：真人秀节目的影响。

passages.en: Reality shows have come to dominate US television over the past 20 years, notes Eunji Kim from Vanderbilt University. And the overwhelming majority of these have a "rags-to-riches" storyline: they feature ordinary Americans who work hard to achieve great economic success. And while these programmes are regularly among the most-watched shows, news broadcasts—which paint a more realistic view of the economic hardship faced by millions of Americans—get a much smaller proportion of the viewership.
passages.zh: 范德比尔特大学的Eunji Kim指出，过去20年间，真人秀节目已经占据了美国电视节目的主导地位。其中绝大多数节目都有“从贫穷到富有”的故事线：节目展现普通美国人通过努力工作取得巨大的经济成功。尽管这些节目经常跻身收视率最高的节目之列，但新闻节目描绘了数百万美国人所面临的经济困境的更为真实的景象，却只获得了小得多的观众比例。

passages.en: Rags-to-riches stories are ubiquitous(无处不在的) on TV—but does watching these programmes actually convince people that economic mobility is easily attainable? To find out, Kim's team had participants watch a 5-minute clip from a reality show with a rags-to-riches storyline. Control participants watched a clip from a reality show that didn't have a rags-to-riches story. After watching the shows, participants rated how much they agreed with four statements relating to the American Dream.
passages.zh: 电视上“从贫穷到富有”的故事无处不在——但观看这些节目真的会让人相信经济流动是很容易实现的吗？为了弄清这一点，Kim的团队让参与者观看一段时长5分钟、讲述“从贫穷到富有”故事的真人秀片段。对照组参与者观看了一段没有“从贫穷到富有”故事的真人秀片段。节目结束后，参与者对四项与美国梦相关的陈述进行认同程度评价。

passages.en: The results showed that those who'd watched a rags-to-riches clip did indeed have a significantly greater belief in the American Dream. Interestingly, when participants were separated by party affiliation, this effect was significant among Republicans but not Democrats, suggesting that the kind of messages implicit in these TV shows may play into people's existing socioeconomic beliefs.
passages.zh: 结果显示，观看了“从贫穷到富有”片段的人确实对美国梦有明显更强的信念。有趣的是，当按照党派归属对参与者进行区分时，这一影响在共和党人中具有显著性，而在民主党人中则没有显著性，这表明这些电视节目所隐含的信息可能会迎合人们已有的社会经济观念。

passages.en: Kim also conducted a survey of 3,000 US residents. They also rated the extent to which they believed success in life is related to various internal factors (such as ambition) and external factors (such as family wealth). Finally, they read a list of TV programmes and indicated which they regularly watched.
passages.zh: Kim还对3000名美国居民进行了调查。他们还评价了自己在多大程度上认为人生成功与各种内在因素（如抱负）和外在因素（如家庭财富）有关。最后，他们阅读了一份电视节目清单，并指出自己经常观看其中哪些节目。

passages.en: Participants who were heavy viewers of rags-to-riches programmes or frequent viewers had a stronger belief in the American Dream than those who never watched such shows.
passages.zh: 经常观看“从贫穷到富有”节目的参与者，比从不观看这类节目的参与者更坚信美国梦。

passages.en: Kim concludes that "rags-to-riches entertainment media are an important cultural force that promotes and perpetuates beliefs in upward mobility". And here's the problem: if people mistakenly believe that hard work is all that is needed for individuals to make a better life for themselves, they may be less supportive of policies that could actually combat inequality.
passages.zh: Kim总结道：“讲述‘从贫穷到富有’故事的娱乐媒体是一股重要的文化力量，它推动并延续了人们对向上流动性的信念。”而问题就在于：如果人们错误地认为，个人要想让自己的生活变得更好，只需要努力工作就够了，那么他们可能就不太支持那些实际上能够应对不平等的政策。

passages.en: "In this era of choice, entertainment media is what captures hearts and minds," Kim writes. "Its political consequences are anything but trivial".
passages.zh: Kim写道：“在这个选择多样的时代，娱乐媒体最能俘获人心、影响思想。它所产生的政治后果绝非无足轻重。”

questions.stem: What do we learn from the passage about young Americans of today?
questions.stem_zh: 从文章中我们了解到当今美国年轻人的什么情况?

options.text: They have greater ambitions than their parents.
options.zh: 他们比父母有更大的抱负。

options.text: They find it difficult to achieve upward mobility.
options.zh: 他们发现实现向上流动很困难。

options.text: They have overtaken their parents in terms of earnings.
options.zh: 他们在收入方面已经超过了父母。

options.text: They envy the opportunities in other industrialised nations.
options.zh: 他们羡慕其他工业化国家的机会。

questions.判型: What do we learn from the passage about young Americans of today 明确问的是关于某个具体群体的事实信息，没有出现 infer / imply / mainly about 等推断或主旨信号。
questions.拆句: 题干主干是 What do we learn from the passage about young Americans of today？about 引导的介宾短语限定 learn 的对象。介词 about 把『青年美国人』锁为定位词，结构平铺无陷阱。
questions.定位: P1 And yet, young Americans today are struggling to earn more than their parents did at the same age, and upward mobility in the US actually compares unfavourably to that of other industrialised nations. 然而，今天的美国年轻人正在艰难地试图挣得比父辈同龄时更多的收入，而且美国的向上流动性事实上比其他工业化国家逊色。

locate.en: And yet, young Americans today are struggling to earn more than their parents did at the same age, and upward mobility in the US actually compares unfavourably to that of other industrialised nations.
locate.zh: 然而，今天的美国年轻人正在艰难地试图挣得比父辈同龄时更多的收入，而且美国的向上流动性事实上比其他工业化国家逊色。

option_analysis.note: 原文只说他们在收入上难超父辈，从未比较两代人的『抱负』。
预判结论是『难以向上流动』，选项 B 几乎是这句话的字面化，二者构成最直接的同义替换。

pairs.opt: find it difficult to achieve upward mobility

pairs.orig: upward mobility in the US actually compares unfavourably

questions.stem: What does Kim's team find about reality TV shows in America?
questions.stem_zh: Kim的团队对美国真人秀节目有什么发现?

options.text: They reinterpret the essence of the popular rags-to-riches culture.

options.text: They urge people to achieve economic success through hard work.
options.zh: 它们敦促人们通过努力工作获得经济成功。

options.text: They help strengthen people's conviction in the American Dream.
options.zh: 它们帮助增强人们对美国梦的信念。

options.text: They feature ordinary Americans striving for social recognition.
options.zh: 它们以普通美国人争取社会认可为特色。

questions.判型: What does Kim’s team find about reality TV shows in America 问的是研究团队的具体发现，是对原文实验结论的事实性提问。
questions.拆句: 主干 What does Kim’s team find about reality TV shows，about 引出研究对象。结构干净，无从句无陷阱。
questions.定位: P5 The results showed that those who'd watched a rags-to-riches clip did indeed have a significantly greater belief in the American Dream. 结果显示，那些看过『白手起家』短片的人确实显著加深了对美国梦的信仰。

locate.en: The results showed that those who'd watched a rags-to-riches clip did indeed have a significantly greater belief in the American Dream.
locate.zh: 结果显示，那些看过『白手起家』短片的人确实显著加深了对美国梦的信仰。

option_analysis.note: 原文只说真人秀展示 rags-to-riches storyline 并验证其加深观众信仰，从未提到节目在『重新诠释』该文化的本质。
they feature ordinary Americans who work hard to achieve great economic success 的主语是节目所呈现的人物在努力，而非节目敦促观众去努力。
预判为『真人秀加深美国梦信仰』，选项 C 把『加深』表达为 help strengthen，把『美国梦信仰』表达为 conviction in the American Dream，二者一一对应。

pairs.orig: significantly greater belief in the American Dream
pairs.opt: help strengthen people’s conviction in the American Dream

option_analysis.note: 原文明确写 great economic success，与选项的 social recognition 不是一回事。

questions.stem: What does the author say about news broadcasts in America?
questions.stem_zh: 作者对美国的新闻广播说了什么?

options.text: They attract far fewer viewers than reality TV.
options.zh: 它们吸引的观众远少于真人秀节目。

options.text: They are bent on reporting the dark side of life.

options.text: They stand in striking contrast with reality TV.
options.zh: 它们与真人秀节目形成鲜明对比。

options.text: They focus on Americans' economic hardships.

questions.判型: What does the author say about news broadcasts in America 问对某具体对象的陈述，没有 infer / suggest，是事实型细节题。
questions.拆句: 主干 What does the author say about news broadcasts in America。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
questions.定位: P3 And while these programmes are regularly among the most-watched shows, news broadcasts—which paint a more realistic view of the economic hardship faced by millions of Americans—get a much smaller proportion of the viewership. 而尽管这些节目（真人秀）经常位列收视率最高的电视节目之列，新闻播报——它们描绘了数以百万计的美国人所面临的经济困境这一更现实的图景——只占据小得多的观众份额。

locate.en: And while these programmes are regularly among the most-watched shows, news broadcasts—which paint a more realistic view of the economic hardship faced by millions of Americans—get a much smaller proportion of the viewership.
locate.zh: 而尽管这些节目（真人秀）经常位列收视率最高的电视节目之列，新闻播报——它们描绘了数以百万计的美国人所面临的经济困境这一更现实的图景——只占据小得多的观众份额。

option_analysis.note: 预判结论是『观众远少于真人秀』，选项 A 把 smaller proportion 改写为 far fewer viewers，把对照对象明示为 reality TV，与定位句的对比关系完全一致。

pairs.orig: get a much smaller proportion of the viewership
pairs.opt: attract far fewer viewers than reality TV

option_analysis.note: paint a more realistic view of the economic hardship 只描述了新闻所呈现的内容，并未对新闻的意图作 be bent on（一心要、决意）这种主观倾向判断。
原文用 while 引出对比，但描述对象是『收视份额』，并未对新闻与真人秀做 striking contrast（鲜明反差）的整体定性评价。
paint a more realistic view of the economic hardship 是把经济困境作为更真实图景的一部分来呈现，并未说新闻 focus on（聚焦于）经济困境；况且 Q48 问的是作者对新闻的总评，而 D 只是从句里附带说明的内容。

questions.stem: What can we infer from the passage about Republicans in general?
questions.stem_zh: 从文章中我们可以推断出共和党人总体上的什么情况?

questions.拆句: 主干 What can we infer from the passage about Republicans in general。in general 提示答案不应是局部小结论，而是适用于该群体的整体性推断。
questions.定位: P5 Interestingly, when participants were separated by party affiliation, this effect was significant among Republicans but not Democrats, suggesting that the kind of messages implicit in these TV shows may play into people's existing socioeconomic beliefs. 有趣的是，当按党派分组时，这种效应在共和党人中显著、而在民主党人中不显著，这意味着真人秀里隐含的信息可能契合了人们既有的社会经济观念。

locate.en: Interestingly, when participants were separated by party affiliation, this effect was significant among Republicans but not Democrats, suggesting that the kind of messages implicit in these TV shows may play into people's existing socioeconomic beliefs.
locate.zh: 有趣的是，当按党派分组时，这种效应在共和党人中显著、而在民主党人中不显著，这意味着真人秀里隐含的信息可能契合了人们既有的社会经济观念。

option_analysis.note: 预判结论是『共和党人本就更信美国梦』，选项 A 是这一推断的标准表达。

pairs.orig: this effect was significant among Republicans but not Democrats
pairs.opt: believe strongly in the American Dream

pairs.orig: play into people’s existing socioeconomic beliefs
pairs.opt: believe strongly in the American Dream

option_analysis.note: 原文只比较了党派对美国梦的信念差异，从未提到任一党派的人在 socio-economic ladder 上的实际行动。
when participants were separated by party affiliation 中 party affiliation 只是『按党派分组』的研究操作变量，并未评价共和党人对自己政党的归属感强弱。
原文只说看了 rags-to-riches 短片后，对美国梦信仰加深的效应在共和党人中显著；并未说共和党人比民主党人更常或更多地观看此类节目。

questions.stem: What is stated about people who believe in upward mobility?
questions.stem_zh: 关于相信向上流动的人,文中陈述了什么?

options.text: They are likely to blame the government for their plight.
options.zh: 他们可能会因自己的困境而责怪政府。

options.text: They regard political consequences as anything but trivial.
options.zh: 他们认为政治后果绝非微不足道。

options.text: They respect individuals striving to climb the social ladder.

options.text: They are less likely to approve of policies to fight inequality.

questions.判型: What is stated about people who believe in upward mobility 用 stated 询问对该人群所作的陈述，是细节题。
questions.拆句: 主干 What is stated about people…？被动语态，who believe in upward mobility 是 people 的定语从句，提示要找作者直接说明这类人会怎样的句子。
questions.定位: P8 And here's the problem: if people mistakenly believe that hard work is all that is needed for individuals to make a better life for themselves, they may be less supportive of policies that could actually combat inequality. 问题就在这里：如果人们错误地以为只要努力工作就足以让个人过上更好的生活，他们就可能更不支持那些其实能对抗不平等的政策。

locate.en: And here's the problem: if people mistakenly believe that hard work is all that is needed for individuals to make a better life for themselves, they may be less supportive of policies that could actually combat inequality.
locate.zh: 问题就在这里：如果人们错误地以为只要努力工作就足以让个人过上更好的生活，他们就可能更不支持那些其实能对抗不平等的政策。

option_analysis.note: P8 只说他们更不支持反不平等政策，从未提到他们指责政府或抱怨自身困境。
Its political consequences are anything but trivial 中代词 Its 指向 entertainment media；选项 B 把这一评价偷塞到『相信向上流动者』身上，属于张冠李戴。
原文只说他们因为相信努力万能而更不支持反不平等政策，从未提到他们对其他奋斗者的态度（如尊敬）。
预判结论『更不支持反不平等政策』与选项 D 完全等义，combat 与 fight 是六级阅读高频可互换词。

pairs.opt: less likely to approve of policies to fight inequality

reading2.title: 2024年6月·第2套 英语六级阅读理解（四选一） 第 2 篇 · 51–55 题答案与解析

passages.en: When someone asks us 'what do you do?' we nearly always reply with our occupation. Work, for many of us, is much more than a job. It is the defining aspect of our identity. For many of us it is through our job that we can define ourselves.
passages.zh: 当有人问我们“你是做什么的？”时，我们几乎总是会回答自己的职业。对我们许多人来说，工作远不只是谋生的手段。它是构成我们身份的决定性因素。对我们许多人而言，我们正是通过自己的工作来界定自己。

passages.en: "Without my job I don't know who I am," is a sentence that has been uttered on more than a handful of occasions from my office chair. Indeed, it can be one of the most challenging aspects I work on with clients who have lost or been forced into changing their jobs. This loss provokes an identity crisis much greater than the loss of the job itself.
passages.zh: “没有了工作，我不知道自己是谁。”这句话在我的咨询室里已经被说过不止几次。事实上，对于那些失去工作或被迫更换工作岗位的来访者来说，这可能是我与他们共同面对的最具挑战性的方面之一。这样的失去所引发的身份危机，远比失去工作本身更为严重。

passages.en: One of the things I have come to understand, however, is that our identity is much more complex than we recognise at first glance. If we take the time to reflect we might recognise that as well as our work we can also identify as a friend, a spouse, a son or daughter, a parent, a member of a sports team or religious community. We may recognise that we feel and act differently in these roles and relationships than we do at work. The passive daughter becomes an assertive leader at work. Furthermore, our identities at work are not static. They change over time. I myself have been a shop assistant, a waitress, a student, a graduate, and a clinical psychologist. At each stage my ability to adapt to and develop my career identity has been crucial to my wellbeing. Whilst we like to eliminate uncertainty in our lives at some level we have to manage uncertainty, especially in today's volatile and ever-shifting job market.
passages.zh: 然而，我逐渐明白，我们的身份比乍看之下所意识到的要复杂得多。如果我们花时间反思，就可能会认识到，除了工作之外，我们还可以是朋友、配偶、儿子或女儿、父母、运动队成员或宗教团体成员。我们可能会发现，在这些角色和关系中，我们的感受和行为与工作时有所不同。被动的女儿在工作中会成为坚定果断的领导者。此外，我们在工作中的身份并不是一成不变的，它们会随着时间而改变。我自己曾做过店员、女服务员、学生、大学毕业生和临床心理学家。在每一个阶段，适应并发展自己的职业身份的能力都对我的幸福至关重要。尽管我们喜欢在某种程度上消除生活中的不确定性，但我们必须学会应对不确定性，尤其是在当今这个动荡且不断变化的就业市场中。

passages.en: How we see ourselves is central to the issue of our identity. When we tell ourselves "I'm good at starting projects but not so great at seeing them through" it can become part of our belief system. But if you have the unfortunate experience of an enforced job change you will need to examine those beliefs to see how grounded in reality they are. You will be required to ask yourself how helpful these beliefs are and consider personal change. We can change our beliefs, behaviours and emotional experience at any time through experimentation, practice and conscious self-discipline. In an age where career progression may lead us into new sectors it is ever more important to challenge our sense of self and explore whether you can create a new experience of your identity by changing the beliefs you hold about yourself in order to expand your career options. Ultimately it is you who define who you are. You are only your job if you let it be so.
passages.zh: 我们如何看待自己，是身份问题的核心。当我们对自己说“我擅长启动项目，但不太擅长将项目进行到底”时，这种看法可能会成为我们信念体系的一部分。但是，如果你不幸被迫更换工作，就需要审视这些信念，看看它们是否有现实依据。你需要问问自己，这些信念有多大帮助，并考虑进行个人改变。我们可以随时通过尝试、练习和有意识的自律来改变自己的信念、行为和情感体验。在职业发展可能把我们带入新领域的时代，挑战自我认知、探索是否能够通过改变对自己的看法来创造新的身份体验，从而拓展职业选择，变得愈发重要。归根结底，定义你是谁的人是你自己。只有当你允许它如此时，你才仅仅是你的工作。

questions.stem: What do we learn from the passage about one's loss of a job?
questions.stem_zh: 从文章中我们了解到关于失业的什么信息?

options.text: It compels them to visit a clinical psychologist.
options.zh: 它迫使他们去看临床心理医生。

questions.判型: What do we learn from the passage about one's loss of a job? 指向一个具体事实——失业会带来什么——并未问推断或主旨。
questions.拆句: 主干 What do we learn from the passage 中 we 是主语、learn 是谓语；about one's loss of a job 是 learn 的范围介词短语，指明问的对象是「失去工作这件事」。句式平铺直叙，无陷阱。

Indeed, it can be one of the most challenging aspects I work on with clients who have lost or been forced into changing their jobs. This loss provokes an identity crisis much greater than the loss of the job itself. 「没有了工作，我就不知道自己是谁」——这话在我办公室的椅子上不止一次被来访者说出。事实上，与那些失去或被迫更换工作的来访者一起处理这种感受，是我工作中最具挑战的部分之一。这种失落所引发的身份危机，要远远大于失业本身。

locate.en: "Without my job I don't know who I am," is a sentence that has been uttered on more than a handful of occasions from my office chair. Indeed, it can be one of the most challenging aspects I work on with clients who have lost or been forced into changing their jobs. This loss provokes an identity crisis much greater than the loss of the job itself.
locate.zh: 「没有了工作，我就不知道自己是谁」——这话在我办公室的椅子上不止一次被来访者说出。事实上，与那些失去或被迫更换工作的来访者一起处理这种感受，是我工作中最具挑战的部分之一。这种失落所引发的身份危机，要远远大于失业本身。

option_analysis.note: 原文只是说作者本人是 clinical psychologist 处理来访者的身份危机，并未要求 visit a clinical psychologist；A 把作者视角偷换成失业者的行为。
原文段 2 并未说失业「提供了扮演不同角色的机会」；段 3 才谈多重身份，但与「失业带来什么」是两个话题。
预判的「不知道自己是谁」与 It renders them puzzled about who they are 在主语、谓语致使关系、宾语状态上完全对应，确定 C。

pairs.orig: Without my job I don't know who I am
This loss provokes an identity crisis

option_analysis.note: 原文谈的是 identity crisis 与重新审视自我信念，并没有说失业必然要 redefine their life's goals，把身份层面的事推到了「人生目标」的宏大命题上。

questions.stem: What has the author come to understand about our identity?
questions.stem_zh: 作者对我们的身份认同有了什么理解?

options.text: It is crucial to our emotional wellbeing.
options.zh: 它对我们的情感健康至关重要。

options.text: It plays a big role in many facets of life.
options.zh: 它在生活的许多方面发挥重要作用。

options.text: It reflects our changing status in society.
options.zh: 它反映了我们在社会中不断变化的地位。

options.text: It is more complicated than it appears.
options.zh: 它比表面看起来更复杂。

questions.判型: What has the author come to understand about our identity? 指向原文一句明确表述，不要求跨段推理。
questions.拆句: 完成时 What has the author come to understand 用 has come to understand 强调认知过程已完成；about our identity 指明认知对象。结构简单。
questions.定位: P3 One of the things I have come to understand, however, is that our identity is much more complex than we recognise at first glance. 然而，我逐渐明白的一件事是：我们的身份远比乍看之下复杂得多。

locate.en: One of the things I have come to understand, however, is that our identity is much more complex than we recognise at first glance.
locate.zh: 然而，我逐渐明白的一件事是：我们的身份远比乍看之下复杂得多。

option_analysis.note: 原文段 3 后半句说 my ability to adapt to and develop my career identity has been crucial to my wellbeing，主语是「适应身份的能力」，并非身份本身；A 把「能力对幸福重要」偷换成「身份对情绪幸福重要」。
原文确实列了多种身份角色，但作者「come to understand」的核心是「身份复杂」这一判断，而非「身份在生活方方面面起作用」；B 只描述现象，未答出认知本身。
原文 They change over time 谈的是「我们在不同时期的身份变化」（学生、毕业生、咨询师等），并非社会地位的变化；C 偷偷加上了 status in society。
预判要点「复杂」「超出表面认知」两块在 more complicated than it appears 里一一落地，无遗漏，确定 D。

pairs.orig: much more complex than we recognise at first glance

questions.stem: What does the passage say about our identities at work?
questions.stem_zh: 文章关于我们在工作中的身份认同说了什么?

options.text: They are essential to our self-esteem.
options.zh: 它们对我们的自尊至关重要。

options.text: They evolve with the passage of time.
options.zh: 它们随着时间的推移而演变。

options.text: They overrule all other self-perceptions.
options.zh: 它们凌驾于所有其他自我认知之上。

options.text: They are key to understanding ourselves.
options.zh: 它们是理解我们自己的关键。

questions.判型: What does the passage say about our identities at work? 让考生回原文找关于「职场身份」的明示句。
questions.拆句: What does the passage say about our identities at work：say 是谓语、about 引出宾语对象；our identities at work 中 at work 修饰 identities，限定「工作中的」身份。无难点。
questions.定位: P3 Furthermore, our identities at work are not static. They change over time. 此外，我们在工作中的身份并非一成不变。它们会随时间而变化。

locate.en: Furthermore, our identities at work are not static. They change over time.
locate.zh: 此外，我们在工作中的身份并非一成不变。它们会随时间而变化。

option_analysis.note: 原文谈的是 wellbeing、identity crisis，没有 self-esteem（自尊）的概念，A 属于原文未提的新信息。
预判「随时间而变」直接命中 They evolve with the passage of time，主谓宾全对应，定 B。

pairs.opt: They evolve with the passage of time

option_analysis.note: 段 3 强调的是身份的「多元」与「变化」，并未说工作身份压倒其他身份；恰相反，作者承认我们还可作为朋友、配偶等存在。
「身份是理解自己的关键」与 Q52 的「身份很复杂」更接近，但题问的是 our identities at work 的具体属性；D 没有答出「随时间而变」这一具体属性。

questions.stem: What do we have to do in today's ever-changing job market?
questions.stem_zh: 在当今不断变化的就业市场中我们必须做什么?

options.text: Strive to develop our social identity.
options.zh: 努力发展我们的社会身份。

options.text: Prepare for different career paths.
options.zh: 为不同的职业道路做准备。

options.text: Try to be assertive at all times.
options.zh: 始终努力保持自信果断。

options.text: Learn to manage uncertainty.
options.zh: 学会管理不确定性。

questions.判型: What do we have to do in today's ever-changing job market? 指向原文一句给出具体动作的陈述。
questions.拆句: What do we have to do in today's ever-changing job market?：do 是询问的动作；in 引导的状语 in today's ever-changing job market 限定背景。句式直白。
questions.定位: P3 Whilst we like to eliminate uncertainty in our lives at some level we have to manage uncertainty, especially in today's volatile and ever-shifting job market. 尽管我们倾向于消除生活中的不确定性，但在某种程度上我们必须学会管理不确定性，尤其是在如今这个动荡多变的就业市场中。

locate.en: Whilst we like to eliminate uncertainty in our lives at some level we have to manage uncertainty, especially in today's volatile and ever-shifting job market.
locate.zh: 尽管我们倾向于消除生活中的不确定性，但在某种程度上我们必须学会管理不确定性，尤其是在如今这个动荡多变的就业市场中。

option_analysis.note: 原文谈 career identity / our identities at work，从未出现 social identity；A 凭空替换了限定语。
「为不同职业路径做准备」更接近段 4 的 career progression / new sectors，但 Q54 问的是动荡市场下「必须做的事」，原文给的明确答案是 manage uncertainty。
原文只是举例说有人在职场会变得 assertive，并未要求所有人 at all times 都要果断；C 把范围扩到全部场景，与原文不符。
predict 的「学会管理不确定性」与 Learn to manage uncertainty 字面几乎一致，确定 D。

questions.stem: What should we do to expand our career options?
questions.stem_zh: 为了拓展职业选择我们应该做什么?

options.text: Alter our perceptions of ourselves.
options.zh: 改变我们对自己的认知。

options.text: Compare various job opportunities.
options.zh: 比较各种工作机会。

options.text: Look into newly emerging sectors.
options.zh: 关注新兴行业领域。

options.text: Exercise self-discipline consciously.
options.zh: 有意识地进行自我约束。

questions.判型: What should we do to expand our career options? 求一个明确的应对动作。
questions.拆句: What should we do to expand our career options?：should we do 是主干，to expand our career options 是目的状语，说明动作要服务的目标。结构平铺直叙。
questions.定位: P4 In an age where career progression may lead us into new sectors it is ever more important to challenge our sense of self and explore whether you can create a new experience of your identity by changing the beliefs you hold about yourself in order to expand your career options. 在一个职业发展可能把我们带入新行业的时代，挑战我们对自我的认知、并探索是否能通过改变你对自己持有的信念来创造一种新的身份体验、以拓宽你的职业选择，变得越来越重要。

locate.en: In an age where career progression may lead us into new sectors it is ever more important to challenge our sense of self and explore whether you can create a new experience of your identity by changing the beliefs you hold about yourself in order to expand your career options.
locate.zh: 在一个职业发展可能把我们带入新行业的时代，挑战我们对自我的认知、并探索是否能通过改变你对自己持有的信念来创造一种新的身份体验、以拓宽你的职业选择，变得越来越重要。

option_analysis.note: 预判要点「改变自我信念」在 Alter our perceptions of ourselves 中以同义改写完整呈现，确定 A。

pairs.orig: changing the beliefs you hold about yourself

option_analysis.note: 原文谈的是「改变信念以扩展选择」，并非 Compare various job opportunities；B 把心理层面的动作偷换为外部信息搜集行为。
原文 career progression may lead us into new sectors 只是时代背景描述，作者并未让读者去 Look into newly emerging sectors。
原文 through experimentation, practice and conscious self-discipline 只是改变信念的途径之一；题干问的是「为扩展职业选择」最直接该做的事，作者明确给出的是改变信念，而非单独突出自律。

translation.title: 2024年6月·第2套英语六级汉译英（段落翻译） · 客观介绍竹子在中国的分布、用途与文化象征 参考译文与解析
translation.directions: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to translate a passage from Chinese into English. You should write your answer on Answer Sheet 2.
translation.source_zh: 中国盛产竹子，是最早开发利用竹资源的国家。竹子在中国分布广泛，品种丰富。竹子实用性强，用于生产和生活的许多方面，如筷子、桌椅的制作和桥梁、房屋的建造。中国人爱竹，自古以来就有无数文人以竹为主题，创作了绚丽多彩的文学和绘画作品。竹子主干(stem) 笔直，象征正直的品格。竹子具有强大的生命力和适应能力，无论环境多么恶劣，都能够顽强生存，因而寓意坚韧不拔的精神。几千年来，竹子一直被视为中华民族品格的象征。
translation.reference_en:
China abounds in bamboo and is among the first countries to develop and utilize bamboo resources. Bamboo is widely distributed across China and comes in a rich variety of species. It is also highly practical and is used in many aspects of production and daily life, such as making chopsticks, tables and chairs, and building bridges and houses. The Chinese people love bamboo, and since ancient times countless scholars have created splendid literary and artistic works with bamboo as their theme. The straight stem of bamboo symbolizes an upright character. Moreover, bamboo has strong vitality and adaptability; no matter how harsh the environment is, it can survive tenaciously, thus symbolizing the spirit of perseverance. For thousands of years, bamboo has been regarded as a symbol of the character of the Chinese nation.
【衔接】
第2、3句同主语 bamboo，第3句改用代词或自然承接第2句 Bamboo is widely distributed… 与第3句 Bamboo is highly practical… 连用同一主语 bamboo，整篇还会多次出现 bamboo。可在部分句改用 It 承接，如第3句写成 It is also highly practical…，并补 also 体现"在分布广之外，还很实用"的递进，避免每句都以 Bamboo 开头显得呆板。
第5、6句象征义之间补衔接，凸显并列第5句讲"笔直象征正直"象征正直的品格、第6句讲"顽强象征坚韧"寓意坚韧不拔的精神，是竹子象征义的两个并列方面。第6句句首可补 Moreover / In addition，显出"除正直外，还象征坚韧"的递进关系，使象征义部分成块。
第7句作全篇收束，用时间状语自然收尾末句 几千年来，竹子一直被视为中华民族品格的象征 是对全篇的总结升华，以 For thousands of years 开头本身就有收束感，无需额外关联词，让它自然作结即可。

main_idea.core: 客观介绍竹子在中国的分布、用途与文化象征
main_idea.detail: 全段是对中国竹文化的客观说明文：先讲资源与分布，再讲实用价值，最后落到象征意义。开篇 中国盛产竹子，是最早开发利用竹资源的国家 即一句客观陈述，属于典型的四六级"中国文化介绍"语体，不带个人叙事色彩，用词应朴实、书面、地道。

tense.detail: 通篇在陈述竹子"长期成立的事实与特征"——分布广、用途多、象征坚韧，都是恒常状态而非某次过去事件，如 竹子在中国分布广泛，品种丰富、竹子实用性强，故全篇以一般现在时为基调；仅"自古创作了作品""几千年来一直被视为"这类跨越历史到今天的句子，才改用过去时或现在完成时。

term_notes.detail: 全篇统一译作 bamboo。注意 bamboo 作"竹子"这一植物总称时为不可数名词，竹子在中国分布广泛 等处一律用单数 bamboo、不加 -s、谓语用单数；只有指"一根根竹竿"实体时才说 bamboo poles。
统一译作 bamboo resources。最早开发利用竹资源的国家 中"资源"指可开发的多种资源，用复数 resources 更自然。
统一译作 the Chinese nation。中华民族品格的象征 取约定俗成的官方译名，前面加定冠词 the。

steps.text: China 作主语，abounds / is 作两个谓语（主语策略：原句主语）中文 中国盛产竹子，是最早开发利用竹资源的国家 两个分句共用同一个主语"中国"，所以英文主语就用 China。前半句核心动词"盛产"译 abounds in / is rich in；后半句"是……国家"用系动词 is + 表语 the country。

"最早开发利用竹资源的"降级成定语从句修饰 country最早开发利用竹资源的国家 里"最早开发利用竹资源"是用来修饰"国家"的一长串定语，照中文塞在 country 前面会很别扭，应降级成后置定语从句 the first country to develop and utilize bamboo resources（用不定式作定语）或 that was among the first to use bamboo resources，挂到 country 后面。

时态回指全篇基调，用一般现在时：China abounds in bamboo and is the first country…，陈述长期事实。 搭配"盛产"用 abound in 或 be rich in；abound 是不及物动词，必须接介词 in，写成 China abounds in bamboo，不能说 abounds bamboo。 单复数bamboo 作植物总称不可数，用单数；"竹资源"含多种资源用复数 bamboo resources。
China abounds in bamboo and is among the first countries to develop and utilize bamboo resources.
Bamboo 作主语，is 系动词带两个并列表语（主语策略：原句主语）竹子在中国分布广泛，品种丰富 两个分句都在描述竹子的状态，主语都是"竹子"，用 Bamboo 作主语；"分布广泛"译 is widely distributed，"品种丰富"译 comes in rich varieties / has a great variety of species。

两个并列描述用 with 或 and 合成一句"分布广泛"和"品种丰富"是对竹子的两点并列描述，可处理成 Bamboo is widely distributed in China and comes in a rich variety of species；也可把后半句降级成 with 介词短语：Bamboo is widely distributed across China, with a rich variety of species，避免两个短句平铺。
时态长期事实，沿用一般现在时 is / comes。 语态"分布"在英文里习惯用被动 is distributed（竹子是被分布的对象），符合英语被动多于汉语的特点。 单复数varieties / species 表"多个品种"用复数；bamboo 仍作不可数单数，谓语 is、comes 用第三人称单数。
Bamboo is widely distributed across China and comes in a rich variety of species.
Bamboo 作主语，is 系动词带 highly practical（主语策略：原句主语）竹子实用性强 是全句主干，主语"竹子"译 Bamboo，"实用性强"用系表 is highly practical / is very useful。后面"用于……""如……"都是对实用性的展开说明。

"用于"降级成被动分词，"如"举例用 such as 引出用于生产和生活的许多方面 降级成过去分词短语 used in many aspects of production and daily life 作后置定语或状语；如筷子、桌椅的制作和桥梁、房屋的建造 用 such as 引出并列名词短语：such as making chopsticks, tables and chairs, and building bridges and houses，把中文"……的制作/建造"转成动名词 making / building。

时态沿用一般现在时 is、is used，陈述竹子的常态用途。 语态"用于"用被动 is used in（竹子被用于），承受动作的竹子作主语，符合英语习惯。 单复数chopsticks 只有复数形式；tables and chairs、bridges and houses 泛指此类物品均用复数。 并列一致such as 后并列的两组用 and 连接、结构对称：making chopsticks… and building bridges…，动名词形式保持一致。
Bamboo is highly practical and is used in many aspects of production and daily life, such as making chopsticks, tables and chairs, and building bridges and houses.

前半 The Chinese love bamboo；后半 countless scholars 作主语带 have created（主语策略：原句主语）本句含两套主语：中国人爱竹 主语是"中国人"译 The Chinese，谓语 love；自古以来就有无数文人……创作了……作品 主语换成"无数文人"译 countless scholars / men of letters，核心谓语"创作了"译 have created。两套主语分别立主干，用分号或 and 连接。
"以竹为主题"降级成介词短语，"自古以来"作时间状语以竹为主题 降级成介词短语 with bamboo as their theme / on the theme of bamboo 作状语，修饰"创作"；自古以来 译时间状语 since ancient times，因其表"从过去延续至今"，触发后半句用现在完成时 have created。

时态"中国人爱竹"是恒常事实用一般现在时 love；"自古以来……创作了……"由 since ancient times 触发现在完成时 have created（动作从古延续到今、影响仍在），这是本句对全篇基调的合理偏离。 主谓一致The Chinese 表"中国人"这一群体作复数，谓语用 love（非 loves）；countless scholars 复数，谓语 have created。 物主代词"以竹为主题"中"主题"属文人，用 their theme，与主语 scholars 保持一致。
The Chinese people love bamboo, and since ancient times countless scholars have created splendid literary and artistic works with bamboo as their theme.
The stem of bamboo 作主语，is straight 作谓语（主语策略：原句主语）竹子主干(stem) 笔直 主语是"竹子主干"译 The stem of bamboo / Its straight stem，谓语"笔直"用系表 is straight；象征正直的品格 的"象征"译 symbolizes。原文已给提示词 stem，直接采用。

"笔直"与"象征"可合成主干+伴随，或并列两动作两个分句可处理成 The stem of bamboo is straight, symbolizing an upright character（把"象征"降为 -ing 分词作结果状语），或并列 The straight stem of bamboo symbolizes an upright character（把"笔直"提为定语、"象征"作谓语）。后者更凝练，避免两个短句。

时态沿用一般现在时 is / symbolizes，陈述竹子的恒常象征义。 主谓一致主语 The stem（单数）或 The straight stem，谓语用第三人称单数 is / symbolizes（带 -s）。 冠词与用词"正直的品格"译 an upright character / integrity；character 表抽象品格时用单数，前加不定冠词 an upright character。"正直"用 upright / honest，不宜用 straight（straight 指物理笔直）。
The straight stem of bamboo symbolizes an upright character.
Bamboo 作主语，has 作核心谓语（主语策略：原句主语）竹子具有强大的生命力和适应能力 是主干，主语"竹子"译 Bamboo，谓语"具有"译 has，宾语 strong vitality and adaptability。后面"无论环境多么恶劣，都能顽强生存""因而寓意……"是让步与结果的展开。

"无论……恶劣"作让步状语，"因而寓意"用分词或 thus 引出结果无论环境多么恶劣，都能够顽强生存 译成 no matter how harsh the environment is, it can survive tenaciously，作让步状语从句；因而寓意坚韧不拔的精神 用 thus symbolizing the spirit of perseverance（-ing 分词作结果状语）或 and therefore symbolizes…，显出"因而"的因果。

时态全句陈述竹子常态，沿用一般现在时 has、can survive、symbolizes。 让步从句语序no matter how harsh the environment is 用陈述语序（how + 形容词 + 主语 + is），不要写成疑问语序 how harsh is the environment。 不可数名词vitality（生命力）、adaptability（适应能力）、perseverance（坚韧不拔）均为抽象不可数名词，不加复数、一般不加冠词。 用词"恶劣"用 harsh / adverse 修饰 environment；"顽强"用 tenaciously / stubbornly。
Bamboo has strong vitality and adaptability; no matter how harsh the environment is, it can survive tenaciously, thus symbolizing the spirit of perseverance.
